title: Soul Snack #49: How Can I Make Amends for Past Behaviors?
excerpt: Discover a new way of seeing and experiencing the world.
bodyHtml:
Discover a new way of seeing and experiencing the world. Start your journey to multisensory perception HERE

We all carry memories of actions we wish we had done differently. The desire to go back and “fix” the past can feel overwhelming – but is that really the path to healing? In this Soul Snack, Gary Zukav explores the true nature of making amends and why authentic forgiveness and transformation are always rooted in the present moment, not the past.

Gary reveals how feelings of guilt, remorse, and the need for approval stem from a frightened part of our personality, and why seeking forgiveness from others can actually be an attempt to control how they see us.

Instead, he explains that genuine healing begins with becoming aware of your intention now, in this moment.The power to make amends is not found in rewriting the past – it is a conscious choice of love, clarity, and authentic power today.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:43) – Do You Really Need to Revisit the Past?: Gary responds to the question of whether apologizing for past wrongs is necessary and reframes the true meaning of amends.
(01:11) – The Roots of Guilt and Remorse: Discover how guilt, shame, and the need for approval arise from frightened parts of your personality—and why acting from these energies only creates more pain.

(01:56) – The Only Question That Matters Now: Learn why the key to healing is not the past, but the present: What intention are you holding in this moment?

(02:45) – The Trap of Seeking Forgiveness: Gary explains why asking others to forgive you can be a form of manipulation—and how forgiveness must come from within.

(03:25) – Forgiveness as Freedom: Understand forgiveness as the release of a heavy burden, like putting down a suitcase full of bricks, and discover how it frees you to live with authentic power.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge:

This week, reflect on moments when you’ve felt the urge to “fix” the past by seeking forgiveness or approval.

Pause and ask yourself:

  1. Am I trying to change someone else so I can feel better – or am I acting from love in this present moment?
    • Notice how your body feels when guilt or shame arises, and then experiment with shifting your intention toward connection and authentic power.
